newsitem.title: USA: American Airlines says talks with pilots slow.
newsitem.headline: American Airlines says talks with pilots slow.

text.p: American Airlines said Wednesday that talks with its pilots were going slowly but it thought both sides wanted an agreement to avert a strike set for midnight Friday.

The comment by American Airlines spokesman Chris Chaimes followed comments by a federal mediator who said talks were going slowly and with "increasing difficulty." A spokesman for the Allied Pilots Association said "there has been no progress so far" and that the union thought a strike remained more likely than not.
Chaimes, asked about the crisis talks, said "they are going slowly, but there is still a lot of time to get a deal and we continue to think both parties want to."

American Airlines raised its wage offer 6 percent increases over four years, up from 5 percent, but the pilots rejected it. The union has asked for an 11.5 percent increase. Another American official said the union had not made a counteroffer and that "the ball is now in the union's court."

The American official noted that the union was concerned it might lose jobs if American went ahead with its plan to buy small jets for its regional airline, American Eagle, and used lower-paid pilots from another union to fly them.
The official said American would try to write some "trust" into a contract promising not to cut pilots and to limit the number of smaller jets it buys for American Eagle.
